function.description: This function is used to create a recommendation model using a given user data and an algorithm type Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

user_data.description: A data frame of user ratings. Rows represent users, columns represent items, and entries represent user ratings for items

algorithm.description: The algorithm to be used for creating the recommendation model. Collaborative filtering, content-based filtering and hybrid filtering.

matrix_factorization.description: Optional parameter to indicate whether matrix factorization should be used. Default is False.

Below is a practical, step‑by‑step guide you can follow to build a modern, production‑ready frontend for your e‑commerce site. I’ll cover the whole pipeline—from choosing a tech stack to deploying and monitoring—so you can pick the parts that fit your team’s skill set and your product’s needs. --- ## 1. Clarify the Scope & Gather Requirements | What | Why | How | |------|-----|-----| | **Core Features** | Shopping cart, product catalog, checkout, user accounts, admin panel, reviews, search, filters, recommendations | List them in a product backlog; prioritize by business value | | **Target Devices** | Desktop, tablet, mobile | Decide if you need a PWA, native app, or just responsive web | | **Performance Goals** | Page load < 2 s, 90 % of users reach checkout within 5 s | Set KPIs early; use Lighthouse or WebPageTest benchmarks | | **Compliance** | PCI‑DSS, GDPR, WCAG 2.1 AA | Document data flows, privacy policy, accessibility checklist | > **Tip:** Create a *feature map* (e.g., a Trello board) so everyone sees what’s coming next. --- ## 2. Choose Your Frontend Stack | Option | Pros | Cons | Typical Use‑Case | |--------|------|------|------------------| | **React + Next.js** | SSR/SSG, rich ecosystem, great for SEO, static export | Learning curve for hooks, SSR complexity | High‑traffic storefronts, content‑heavy sites | | **Vue + Nuxt.js** | Simpler learning curve, flexible, SSR/SSG | Smaller community than React | MVPs, teams already comfortable with Vue | | **Angular** | Opinionated, built‑in DI, RxJS | Heavyweight, steeper learning | Enterprise‑grade apps, internal tooling | | **SvelteKit** | Compiles away framework, tiny bundle size | Smaller ecosystem, less mature | Performance‑critical sites, small teams | ### Recommendation If you’re starting fresh and want a balance between performance, SEO, and developer experience, **React + Next.js** is a solid choice. It gives you: - Server‑Side Rendering (SSR) for SEO - Static Site Generation (SSG) for fast pages - Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR) for dynamic content - Built‑in API routes for simple backend logic --- ## 3. Design & Prototyping | Tool | Why | How | |------|-----|-----| | **Figma / Sketch / Adobe XD** | Collaborative design, component libraries | Create wireframes → high‑fidelity mockups → interactive prototypes | | **Storybook** | Component documentation & testing | Build UI components in isolation, share with designers | | **Zeplin / Avocode** | Handoff to developers | Export specs, CSS, assets | **Process** 1. **User Flow Mapping** – Map out the journey from landing page → product detail → cart → checkout → confirmation. 2. **Component Library** – Define reusable components: `Button`, `Card`, `Modal`, `ProductGrid`, `CartSidebar`. 3. **Design Tokens** – Centralize colors, spacing, typography in a JSON file; use a CSS-in-JS solution or Tailwind CSS to consume them. --- ## 4. Project Setup ```bash # Create a new Next.js app npx create-next-app@latest ecommerce-frontend --typescript cd ecommerce-frontend # Add Tailwind CSS (or your preferred styling) npm install -D tailwindcss postcss autoprefixer npx tailwindcss init -p # Add component library (optional) npm i @mui/material @emotion/react @emotion/styled ``` **Folder Structure** ``` /components # Reusable UI components /pages # Next.js pages (routes) /styles # Global styles, Tailwind config /lib # Utilities, hooks, API clients /store # Redux Toolkit / Zustand / Recoil /tests # Jest + React Testing Library ``` --- ## 5. State Management | Library | When to Use | |---------|-------------| | **Redux Toolkit** | Complex global state, many reducers | | **Zustand** | Simple, lightweight store | | **Recoil** | Fine‑grained atom state, derived selectors | | **React Context + useReducer** | Small projects, no external dependency | **Example (Zustand)** ```ts // lib/store.ts import create from 'zustand'; export const useCartStore = create((set) => ({ items: [] as CartItem[], addItem: (item: CartItem) => set(state => ({ items: [...state.items, item] })), removeItem: (id: string) => set(state => ({ items: state.items.filter(i => i.id !== id) })), })); ``` --- ## 6. API Integration | Approach | Pros | Cons | |----------|------|------| | **REST** | Simple, widely understood | Requires multiple endpoints | | **GraphQL** | Single endpoint, flexible queries | Adds complexity, caching overhead | | **Serverless Functions** (Next.js API routes) | No separate backend, easy scaling | Limited compute time, cold starts | **Example (Next.js API route)** ```ts // pages/api/products/[id].ts import { NextApiRequest, NextApiResponse } from 'next'; import { getProductById } from '../../../lib/db'; export default async function handler(req: NextApiRequest, res: NextApiResponse) { const { id } = req.query; const product = await getProductById(id as string); if (!product) return res.status(404).json({ error: 'Not found' }); res.json(product); } ``` --- ## 7. Routing & Navigation - **Dynamic Routes** – `/products/[slug]` for product pages. - **Nested Layouts** – Use Next.js `app/` directory for layout composition. - **Breadcrumbs** – Show navigation hierarchy for SEO and UX. --- ## 8. Authentication & Authorization | Method | Where to Store | Security Notes | |--------|----------------|----------------| | **JWT** | HttpOnly cookie | Protect against XSS, CSRF | | **OAuth2** | Redirect flow | Use PKCE for SPA | | **Auth0 / Firebase Auth** | Managed service | Offloads compliance | **Implementation (Next.js + Auth0)** ```ts // lib/auth0.ts import { initAuth0 } from '@auth0/nextjs-auth0'; export const auth0 = initAuth0({ domain: process.env.AUTH0_DOMAIN!, clientId: process.env.AUTH0_CLIENT_ID!, clientSecret: process.env.AUTH0_CLIENT_SECRET!, scope: 'openid profile email', redirectUri: process.env.REDIRECT_URI!, postLogoutRedirectUri: process.env.POST_LOGOUT_REDIRECT_URI!, }); ``` --- ## 9. Shopping Cart & Checkout Flow 1. **Add to Cart** – Update local store + sync with server (optimistic UI). 2. **Persist Cart** – Store in localStorage or cookie for guest users. 3. **Checkout** – Use a payment gateway (Stripe, PayPal, Braintree). 4. **Order Confirmation** – Show order summary, send email via webhook. **Stripe Integration (Next.js API route)** ```ts // pages/api/checkout.ts import { NextApiRequest, NextApiResponse } from 'next'; import Stripe from 'stripe'; const stripe = new Stripe(process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY!, { apiVersion: '2023-10-16' }); export default async function handler(req: NextApiRequest, res: NextApiResponse) { const { items, email } = req.body; const lineItems = items.map((i: any) => ({ price_data: { currency: 'usd', product_data: { name: i.name }, unit_amount: i.price * 100, }, quantity: i.quantity, })); const session = await stripe.checkout.sessions.create({ payment_method_types: ['card'], line_items: lineItems, mode: 'payment', customer_email: email, success_url: `${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/success?session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}`, cancel_url: `${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/cancel`, }); res.json({ url: session.url }); } ``` --- ## 10. Performance Optimizations | Technique | How | |-----------|-----| | **Image Optimization** | Use Next.js `` component, lazy loading, WebP | | **Code Splitting** | Automatic with Next.js; use dynamic imports for heavy modules | | **Prefetching** | `next/link` prefetches pages on hover | | **Caching** | CDN edge caching, HTTP cache headers, SWR for data fetching | | **Critical CSS** | Extract with `next/font` or `styled-components` SSR | | **Bundle Analysis** | `next-bundle-analyzer` to spot large dependencies | --- ## 11. Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA) | Checklist | Implementation | |-----------|----------------| | Semantic HTML | Use `
`, `
`, `
`, `
` | | ARIA Labels | `aria-label`, `role="button"` where needed | | Keyboard Navigation | `tabindex`, focus management | | Color Contrast | Verify contrast ratio > 4.5:1 | | Alt Text | All images have meaningful `alt` attributes | | Skip Links | `Skip to main content` | Run automated tests with **axe-core** or **jest-axe**. --- ## 12. Testing Strategy | Layer | Tool | Example | |-------|------|---------| | Unit | Jest + React Testing Library | Test component rendering | | Integration | Cypress | End‑to‑end checkout flow | | Visual Regression | Percy | Detect UI regressions | | Performance | Lighthouse CI | Automated performance audits | **Example (Jest + RTL)** ```ts // __tests__/components/ProductCard.test.tsx import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react'; import ProductCard from '../../components/ProductCard'; test('renders product title', () => { render(); expect(screen.getByText(/Cool T‑Shirt/i)).toBeInTheDocument(); }); ``` --- ## 13. Deployment & CI/CD | Platform | Key Features | |----------|--------------| | **Vercel** | Native Next.js support, preview deployments | | **Netlify** | Edge functions, split testing | | **AWS Amplify** | Full‑stack hosting, GraphQL API | | **Docker + Kubernetes** | Custom infrastructure, microservices | **CI Pipeline (GitHub Actions)** ```yaml name: CI on: push: branches: [main] pull_request: jobs: build-test: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: actions/setup-node@v4 with: node-version: '20' - run: npm ci - run: npm run lint - run: npm test - run: npm run build ``` --- ## 14. Monitoring & Analytics | Tool | Purpose | |------|---------| | **Google Analytics / GA4** | Traffic, conversion funnels | | **Hotjar** | Heatmaps, session recordings | | **Sentry** | Runtime error tracking | | **LogRocket** | Session replay, performance insights | | **New Relic** | Full‑stack performance monitoring | Set up **Sentry** in Next.js: ```ts // lib/sentry.ts import * as Sentry from '@sentry/nextjs'; Sentry.init({ dsn: process.env.SENTRY_DSN!, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, }); ``` --- ## 15. Documentation & Knowledge Transfer - **README** – Project setup, scripts, environment variables. - **Contributing.md** – Code style guidelines, commit conventions. - **Architecture.md** – High‑level diagram, component responsibilities. - **API Docs** – Swagger/OpenAPI spec or Postman collection. --- ## Quick Reference Cheat Sheet | Task | Command / Code | |------|----------------| | Start dev server | `npm run dev` | | Build for production | `npm run build` | | Lint | `npm run lint` | | Run tests | `npm test` | | Deploy to Vercel | `vercel --prod` | | Generate sitemap | `next-sitemap` plugin | --- ## Final Thoughts 1. **Start Small** – Build a minimal viable product (MVP) with core features, then iterate. 2. **Automate Everything** – CI/CD, linting, testing, performance checks. 3. **Keep UX in Mind** – Fast, accessible, and intuitive interfaces drive conversions. 4. **Stay Modular** – Components, hooks, and stores should be reusable across pages. 5. **Monitor & Iterate** – Use analytics and error tracking to continuously improve. Feel free to ask for deeper dives into any of the sections—whether it’s setting up a specific API route, configuring a payment gateway, or writing unit tests for your cart logic. Happy coding!
